lessons.title: Save, name and find your files
lessons.text:
Make a folder, give a file a name the next person can understand, save it in the right place and find it again.
Steps checked on Windows 11 with File Explorer, Word for Microsoft 365 and OneDrive, 2026-11-06. On a Mac, a tablet or a shared training computer the buttons may sit in a different place. Ask your instructor where class work is saved.
Why this matters on the job
On a BC job site, a foreman may send you a tool list, a safety form or a set of drawings and ask for it back by the end of the day. If you save it as "Document1" on the desktop, nobody can find it, and that includes you next week. A good file name and the right folder save time and stop people working from an old copy.
Key ideas
Device, app, file and folder. The device is the equipment: a laptop, tablet or phone. An app is the program you use, such as Word. A file is one saved piece of work, such as a letter or a spreadsheet. A folder holds files, the way a job box holds tools.
Name and location are two different things. The name tells you what the file is. The location tells you where it is saved. You need both to find it again.
A good file name says what the file is, which job it belongs to and the date or version. For example:
tool-list_riverbend-job_2026-11-06_v1
Use words a co-worker would search for.
Put the date year first (2026-11-06) so files sort in date order.
Use v1, v2 to tell versions apart. Before editing, save a copy with the new version name so the earlier version stays unchanged, even when AutoSave is on.
Windows does not allow these characters in a name: < > : " / \ | ? *. OneDrive does not allow them either.
On this computer or in the cloud. A file saved in a OneDrive folder is stored online and can also sit on the computer. In File Explorer, OneDrive shows a small icon beside each file:
What you see beside the file What it means
Blue cloud outline Online only. It does not take space on the computer, and you cannot open it without the internet.
Green tick Downloaded to this device. You can open it without the internet.
Solid green circle with a white tick Set to "Always keep on this device".
Finding a file. Open File Explorer with the Windows logo key + E. Use the search box in File Explorer to search by name. If you know the folder, go to it first, then search. Windows desktop search can find online-only OneDrive files by name, but it cannot search the words inside them.
Worked example
Devon works for a fictional framing contractor, Riverbend Builders. The foreman emails a blank material request form. Devon:
Opens File Explorer (Windows logo key + E) and goes to Documents.
Selects New > Folder, types Riverbend job, and presses Enter.
Opens the form in Word, fills it in and selects File > Save As.
Browses to the Riverbend job folder.
Types the name material-request_riverbend_2026-11-06_v1 and selects Save.
Closes Word, then finds the file again by typing material-request in the File Explorer search box.
The name tells anyone what the file is, which job and which day. The folder keeps it with the rest of that job's paperwork.
Read the nesting from top to bottom: Documents contains Riverbend job, which contains material-request_riverbend_2026-11-06_v1. The name identifies the work; the folder path is its location. This is a folder diagram, not a screenshot. Open the full-size diagram.
Practice
Use the practice folder your instructor gives you. Use invented job names only. Do not open other people's files.
Task 1 (level 1) Match each word to its meaning: device, app, file, folder.
Word Meaning
One saved piece of work
A place that holds files
The equipment you hold or sit at
The program you use to do a task
Task 2 (level 1) In your practice location, make a folder named IS4S-digital-[your initials]. Inside it, make a second folder named Riverbend job. Show your instructor both folders.
Task 3 (level 1) Open Word. Type one line: Tool check: 2 tape measures, 1 chalk line, 1 speed square. Save it in Riverbend job with a name that follows the pattern in Key ideas. Write the name and the location you used.
Name: ________
Location: ________
Task 4 (level 1) Close Word. Find your file using the File Explorer search box. Open it and check that your line of text is there.
Task 5 (level 2) Before changing the list, save a copy with v2 in its name using Save As or Save a Copy. Check that you are working in v2, then add 1 utility knife and save. Close the file. Open both versions and check that v1 is unchanged and only v2 has the knife. Copying before editing protects v1 when AutoSave is on.
Task 6 (level 1) Each of these names has a problem. Write a better name for each one.
Document1
final final NEW
drawings: unit 4?
Check yourself
What is the difference between a file's name and its location?
Why put the date year first, as in 2026-11-06?
You see a blue cloud outline beside a file and the internet is down. Can you open it?
Which keys open File Explorer?
Why save a changed file as v2 instead of saving over v1?

lessons.title: Keyboard, mouse and touch screen
lessons.text:
Sit and type in a way that protects your wrists, use the shortcuts that save the most time, type accented letters and use a touch screen.
Shortcuts checked on Windows 11 and Word for Microsoft 365, 2026-11-06. Touch gestures checked for Windows 11 touch screens and touchpads. Phones and tablets use similar gestures, but check your own device.
Why this matters on the job
Trades work now includes typed daily reports, time sheets, safety forms on a tablet and messages to the office. Typing with sore wrists or hunting for keys makes a five-minute report take twenty. In BC, sprains and strains are the most common work injury, and a desk set up badly can cause them too. A few habits and a handful of shortcuts make computer work faster and easier on your body.
Key ideas
Sit so the computer fits you
WorkSafeBC's guide How to Make Your Computer Workstation Fit You gives these points for sitting at a computer:
Forearms level, elbows bent about 90 degrees, shoulders relaxed.
Wrists straight. Fingertips at the height of the middle row of keys.
Head upright. The top of the screen about level with your eyes, about an arm's length away.
Feet flat on the floor or on a firm footrest.
Mouse at the same height as the keyboard and close to it. Move the mouse with your whole arm, not by bending your wrist side to side.
Take short breaks. Pauses of 20 seconds to 2 minutes with a stretch help. If your muscles are already sore, you waited too long.
Habits to replace
These are from the ACCESS typing lesson, updated:
Sloppy posture. Slouching throws you off balance, so one hand works harder than the other. You get stiff, fidget and make more mistakes.
Resting your wrists on the desk or keyboard edge while typing. Keep wrists straight and floating while you type. A palm rest is for resting between bursts of typing, with the palm, not the wrist, on the rest.
Looking at your hands or the screen the whole time. You will miss lines or type them twice. Keep your eyes on the paper you are copying from, and check the screen at the end of each line or sentence.
Working through pain. Pain is your body asking for attention. Stop, stretch, change position, and tell your instructor or supervisor if it keeps coming back.
Shortcuts worth learning first
Hold the first key, tap the second, then let go of both.
Shortcut What it does
Ctrl + C Copy what is selected
Ctrl + X Cut what is selected
Ctrl + V Paste
Ctrl + Shift + V Paste text only, without the old formatting
Ctrl + Z Undo the last action
Ctrl + Y Redo (in Word)
Ctrl + A Select everything
Ctrl + S Save
Ctrl + F Find a word in the document
Windows logo key + E Open File Explorer
Windows logo key + . (period) Open the emoji panel
Accented letters in Word
Names and words like résumé, François and Thérèse need accents. In Word and Outlook you press a combination, let go, then type the letter.
To type Press, let go, then type the letter
é, á, í, ó, ú Ctrl + ' (apostrophe)
è, à, ù Ctrl + ` (grave accent, the key left of 1)
ê, â, ô Ctrl + Shift + ^
ä, ë, ö, ü Ctrl + Shift + :
ç Ctrl + , (comma), then c
For any other symbol, Word has a code method: type the character's code, then press Alt + X. For example, 00B0 then Alt + X gives the degree sign °, and 00BD then Alt + X gives ½. Numbers count as part of a code, so if the code comes right after a number, type a space first, press Alt + X, then delete the space.
Touch screens and touchpads
On a Windows touch screen:
To do this Touch screen Touchpad
Select Tap Tap
Scroll Slide two fingers up, down or sideways Slide two fingers
Zoom in or out Pinch two fingers in or spread them out Pinch or spread two fingers
See more commands (like a right-click) Press and hold the item Tap with two fingers, or press the lower-right corner
Worked example
Ravi has to type the accented sentence below into a site report. For "résumé":
Type r.
Press Ctrl + ' together, let go, then type e. Word shows é.
Type sum.
Press Ctrl + ' again, let go, type e.
Result: résumé. If the wrong letter appears, press Ctrl + Z and try again.
Practice
Task 1 (level 1) Sit at your computer. Check yourself against the six points under "Sit so the computer fits you". Change one thing, such as chair height or screen distance. Write what you changed.
Task 2 (level 1) In a blank Word document, type: Bring the 25 ft tape and the chalk line. Then use only shortcuts to:
select the whole line
copy it
paste it twice below
undo the last paste
save the document as shortcut-practice_[initials]_v1
Task 3 (level 1) Type this ACCESS practice passage exactly, with every accent:
Thérèse Mädchen gave François her résumé last Tuesday. She wanted him to check it for errors and make suggestions on improving the format. When François came to see Thérèse today, he returned her retyped résumé along with a small bouquet of flowers and said, "Voilà, here is your new and improved résumé."
Count the accented letters you typed. Write the number.
Task 4 (level 2) A welder's report needs this line. Type it using the Alt + X method for the symbols: Bevel: 37½° on both plates.
Task 5 (level 1) On a touch screen or touchpad, open a long web page or document. Scroll down with two fingers, zoom in on a word, then press and hold (touch screen) or two-finger tap (touchpad) to see the extra menu. Tell a partner which gesture did what.
Task 6 (level 2) Type the Task 3 passage again without looking at your hands. Time yourself for two minutes. Count the words you typed and the mistakes. Write both.
Words: _ Mistakes: _
Check yourself
Where should your wrists be while you type?
What does Ctrl + Z do?
How do you type é in Word?
On a touch screen, how do you get the menu that a right-click would show?
What should you do if your wrist starts to hurt while typing?

lessons.title: Format a work document in Word
lessons.text:
Use the Home tab, heading styles, line spacing and a title page to turn plain text into a workplace procedure people can read and follow.
Steps checked in Word for Microsoft 365 on Windows 11, 2026-11-06. Word for the web, Mac and tablets have the same tabs, but some buttons sit in different places.
Why this matters on the job
Contractors in BC write safe work procedures, toolbox talk notes and site rules in Word. A procedure that looks like one long block of text gets skimmed and ignored. Clear headings, even spacing and bold where it matters make a document people will actually follow, and a screen reader can read it aloud to someone who needs that.
Key ideas
The ribbon and the tabs
Across the top of Word is the ribbon, a band of buttons split into tabs: File, Home, Insert, Design, Layout, References, Mailings, Review, View. The old Word menus (File, Edit, Format) from ACCESS's first computer lessons are gone. Most everyday tools are on the Home tab:
Group on the Home tab Use it to
Font Change font, size, bold, italic, underline, colour
Paragraph Line up text, make lists, set line spacing
Styles Apply headings and body text styles in one click
Editing Find and replace words
Rest the pointer on any button to see its name.
Styles, not hand formatting
A style is a saved set of formatting. Select a line and choose Heading 1 in the Styles gallery on the Home tab, and it gets the heading font, size and spacing in one click. Use Heading 1 for the document title, Heading 2 for section headings, and Normal for body text. Styles keep every heading the same, and screen readers use them to jump between sections. Shortcut: Ctrl + Alt + 1 for Heading 1, Ctrl + Alt + 2 for Heading 2.
Line spacing and space between paragraphs
Line spacing is the gap between lines inside a paragraph. Shortcuts: Ctrl + 1 single, Ctrl + 5 1.5 lines, Ctrl + 2 double.
Space before and after is the gap between paragraphs.
To set both: select the paragraphs, go to Home > Line and Paragraph Spacing, choose Line Spacing Options, pick the Line spacing and set Before and After, then OK.
When a supervisor asks for a document "double-spaced", change the line spacing. Do not press Enter twice between lines. Extra blank lines move around when someone edits the document, and the spacing setting does not.
Other tools you will use today
To do this Use
Centre a line Ctrl + E
Start a new page Ctrl + Enter (page break)
Find a word Ctrl + F
Find and replace Ctrl + H
Turn the page sideways or upright Layout > Orientation, then Landscape or Portrait
Check spelling Review tab
Check that others can read it Review > Check Accessibility
Worked example
Mei has the sentence Lockout before you clear a jam typed in a procedure. She wants it to be a section heading.
She clicks anywhere in the line.
On the Home tab, in Styles, she chooses Heading 2.
The line changes size and colour, and gets space above it. She did not touch the font box.
Later the safety coordinator wants all section headings larger. Mei right-clicks Heading 2 in the Styles gallery and chooses Modify. Every Heading 2 in the document changes at once.
Practice
Open a new blank Word document. Type or paste this text exactly. It is for a fictional contractor.
Tool Crib Sign-Out
Taking a tool
Every hand tool and power tool in the crib has a number. Before you take a tool, write the number, your name and the date on the sign-out sheet.
Checking a tool
Check the tool before you leave the crib. Look for a cracked handle, a frayed cord or a missing guard. Do not take a damaged tool. Tag it and tell the crib attendant.
Returning a tool
Return tools by 3:30 p.m. Wipe them down and coil cords loosely. The attendant checks each tool back in and initials the sheet.
This procedure is for Riverbend Builders, a fictional company used for training.
Task 1 (level 1) Name the Home tab group you would use to: (a) make text bold, (b) apply Heading 1, (c) set 1.5 line spacing, (d) replace one word with another.
Task 2 (level 1) Apply Heading 1 to Tool Crib Sign-Out. Apply Heading 2 to the three section headings.
Task 3 (level 2) Select the four body paragraphs (not the headings). Set line spacing to 1.5 lines and 6 pt After. Delete any blank lines you typed between paragraphs.
Task 4 (level 1) Make the sentence Do not take a damaged tool. bold.
Task 5 (level 2) The return time has changed. Use Find and Replace (Ctrl + H) to change 3:30 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. Then use Find (Ctrl + F) to count matches for tool, including tools, with case matching and whole-word matching off. Do this before adding the title page in Task 6. Write the count Word shows.
Task 6 (level 2) Make a title page. Click at the very start of the document. Type these four lines, each on its own line: Tool Crib Sign-Out, Prepared by [your name], ACCESS Indigenous Skills4Success, Digital, today's date. Centre the four lines with Ctrl + E. Then press Ctrl + Enter so the procedure starts on page 2.
Task 7 (level 1) Turn the page sideways with Layout > Orientation > Landscape. Look at it, then change it back to Portrait. Write which one suits a one-page procedure and why.
Task 8 (level 2) Run Review > Check Accessibility. Read what it finds. Fix anything it lists, or write "no issues found". Save the document as tool-crib-procedure_[initials]_v1 in your Riverbend job folder from Lesson 1.
Check yourself
What is the difference between applying Heading 2 and making text bigger and bold by hand?
Which shortcut gives double line spacing?
Why is it better to use Space After than to press Enter twice between paragraphs?
Where do you turn a page from upright (Portrait) to sideways?
Which tab holds Check Accessibility?

lessons.title: Build a table in Word and save a PDF
lessons.text:
Put information in a simple Word table with a header row, then save a PDF copy that anyone can open and check it before you send it.
Steps checked in Word for Microsoft 365 on Windows 11, 2026-11-06.
Why this matters on the job
Sign-out sheets, crew lists, inspection checklists and material orders are all tables. When you send one to a supplier, an owner or a WorkSafeBC officer, a PDF usually preserves the page layout better than an editable Word file, and the reader does not need Word. Check the PDF before sharing it; a PDF is not automatically accessible or protected from editing. You keep the Word file so you can still edit it.
Key ideas
When to use a table
Use a table for information that lines up in rows and columns, such as "tool number, name, date out, date back". Microsoft's accessibility advice is to keep tables simple:
one header row with a name for every column
no merged or split cells, and no table inside a table
no completely empty rows or columns
Screen readers count cells to keep track of where they are, so merged cells and blank rows confuse them.
Making a table
Click where the table should go.
Insert > Table, then move the pointer over the grid to pick the number of columns and rows, and click.
For a bigger table, choose Insert > Table > Insert Table and type the numbers.
Type in the first cell. Press Tab to move to the next cell, and Shift + Tab to go back.
If the text is already typed with tabs between the parts, select it and choose Insert > Table > Convert Text to Table.
The header row
When the cursor is in a table, two extra tabs appear on the ribbon for table design and table layout. On the table Design tab, in Table Style Options, tick Header Row. This tells Word and screen readers that the first row holds the column names.
Saving a PDF copy
Save the Word file first (Ctrl + S).
Select File > Save a Copy. (For a file never saved before, File > Save As also works.)
Select Browse and choose the folder.
In the file type list, choose PDF.
Select Save.
Then open the PDF and check every page: all rows there, nothing cut off at the edge, headings correct. A PDF can still be opened and changed in some programs, including Word, so it is a reading copy, not a lock.
Worked example
A crew lead at the fictional Riverbend Builders needs a sign-out table for three ladders.
In the procedure document, she clicks below the "Taking a tool" paragraph.
Insert > Table, 3 columns by 4 rows.
She types Tool number, Tab, Name, Tab, Date out in row 1, then the ladder numbers L-01, L-02 and L-03 down the first column.
On the table Design tab she ticks Header Row.
She saves (Ctrl + S), then File > Save a Copy, chooses PDF, and saves ladder-sign-out_riverbend_2026-11-06_v1.pdf.
She opens the PDF and checks that all four rows are there.
Practice
Task 1 (level 1) Which of these would you put in a table? Write yes or no beside each, and one reason.
a list of five tools with serial numbers and the date each was last inspected: ______
a two-paragraph note to the night crew: ______
a weekly schedule of who is on which crew each day: ______
Task 2 (level 2) Open the government page Skill components and proficiency levels at https://www.canada.ca/en/services/jobs/training/initiatives/skills-success/learning-steps.html. In a new Word document, make a table with 3 columns and 10 rows. Header row: Skill, What it means, Example in my trade. Fill one row for each of the nine Skills for Success, using the page for the first two columns and your own trade for the third.
Task 3 (level 1) Tick Header Row on the table Design tab. Then run Review > Check Accessibility and fix anything it lists.
Task 4 (level 2) Open your tool-crib-procedure_[initials]_v1 from Lesson 3. Save a copy as v2 before editing, and confirm v2 is open. Under "Taking a tool", add a table with the columns Tool number, Name, Date out, Date back, and four rows for tools T-01 to T-04 (leave Name and dates for the crew to fill). Save as v2.
Task 5 (level 2) Save a PDF copy of your Task 4 document. Open the PDF. Check the title page, the table and the last line. Write one thing you checked and what you found.
Task 6 (level 2) The text below was typed with a tab between each part. Type it the same way, then turn it into a table with Convert Text to Table.
Item Qty Unit 2x4 stud, 8 ft 48 each Drywall screws 6 box Construction adhesive 12 tube
Check yourself
Why should a table have a header row?
Which key moves you to the next cell?
Why send a PDF instead of the Word file to a supplier?
Why keep the Word file after you make the PDF?
Name one thing to check when you open the PDF.

lessons.title: Build a materials list in Excel
lessons.text:
Enter a job's materials in Excel, work out line totals with formulas, add them with SUM, find an average and watch the totals update when a quantity changes.
Steps checked in Excel for Microsoft 365 on Windows 11, 2026-11-06. Excel for the web and Mac use the same formulas.
Why this matters on the job
Estimators, foremen and small contractors price jobs in Excel. A materials list with formulas does the arithmetic for you and, more importantly, redoes it every time a quantity or price changes. A list where the totals were typed in by hand is wrong the moment the order changes, and nobody can tell.
Key ideas
The parts of a worksheet
A cell is one box. It holds a number, text or a formula.
Columns have letters (A, B, C). Rows have numbers (1, 2, 3).
A cell reference is the column letter then the row number. B3 is column B, row 3.
The formula bar at the top shows what is really in the selected cell, including any formula.
Sheet tabs at the bottom switch between worksheets in the same file (the workbook).
Formulas
Every formula starts with an equal sign (=). After it come numbers or cell references joined by operators:
Operator Meaning Example
+ add =B2+B3
- subtract =E6-E2
* multiply =B2*D2
/ divide =E6/4
Excel has no SUBTRACT function. Use the minus sign.
Press Enter to finish a formula. The cell shows the answer and the formula bar shows the formula.
Order of operations: BEDMAS
Excel follows BEDMAS: Brackets first, then Exponents, then Division and Multiplication from left to right, then Addition and Subtraction from left to right.
=5+2*3 gives 11. Excel multiplies 2 × 3 = 6 first, then adds 5.
=(5+2)*3 gives 21. The brackets make Excel add 5 + 2 = 7 first, then multiply by 3.
If you want something done first, put it in brackets.
Functions: SUM and AVERAGE
A function is a built-in formula. A range like E2:E5 means every cell from E2 down to E5.
=SUM(E2:E5) adds E2, E3, E4 and E5.
=AVERAGE(D2:D5) adds D2 to D5 and divides by how many numbers there are (4).
AutoSum builds a SUM for you: select the empty cell under a column of numbers, then select AutoSum on the Home tab (it is also on the Formulas tab), and press Enter.
Copy a formula with the fill handle
Select a cell with a formula. The small square at its bottom-right corner is the fill handle. Drag it down, and Excel copies the formula, changing the row numbers to match. =B2*D2 in row 2 becomes =B3*D3 in row 3.
Show money as money
Select the cells, then on the Home tab, in the Number group, choose Accounting Number Format. For the Currency format with other choices, press Ctrl + 1 and pick Currency. If a cell shows #####, the column is too narrow for the number. Make the column wider.
Do not type fractions like 1/2 into a number cell. Excel may turn them into a date. Use decimals (0.5) for numbers.
Worked example
Line total for the studs: in E2, type =B2*D2 and press Enter. Excel shows 230.4, because 48 × 4.80 = 230.40. Now change B2 from 48 to 50. E2 changes to 240 by itself. That is the point of a formula. Restore B2 to 48 before starting the practice tasks.
Practice
The prices below are practice numbers for this lesson, not current store prices. The job is for the fictional Riverbend Builders.
A B C D E
1 Item Qty Unit Unit price Line total
2 2x4 stud, 8 ft 48 each 4.80
3 Drywall screws, box of 100 6 box 12.50
4 Construction adhesive 12 tube 7.25
5 Drywall, 1/2 in, 4x8 sheet 30 sheet 18.00
6 Total
7 Average unit price
8 Total with 10% contingency
Task 1 (level 1) Write the cell reference for: (a) the word Qty, (b) the price of construction adhesive, (c) the quantity of drywall sheets.
(a) __ (b) _ (c) ___
Task 2 (level 1) Open a blank workbook. Type the table above into cells A1 to D8, leaving column E empty except for the heading. Save it as materials-list_riverbend_[initials]_v1.xlsx in your Riverbend job folder.
Task 3 (level 2) In E2, enter a formula for the line total of the studs. Use the fill handle to copy it down to E5. Write the four line totals.
E2 __ E3 _ E4 E5 ___
Task 4 (level 2) In E6, use AutoSum to total the four line totals. Write the formula Excel made and the answer.
Task 5 (level 2) In D7, use AVERAGE to find the average unit price of the four items. Write the answer to the nearest cent.
Task 6 (level 2) BEDMAS check. Before you type each formula into an empty cell, write what you think the answer is. Then type it and compare.
Formula Your prediction Excel's answer
=48*4.80+6*12.50
=(48+6)*4.80
=E6*1.1
Put =E6*1.1 into E8 when you are done.
Task 7 (level 1) Format D2:D7 and E2:E8 as money with Accounting Number Format. If you see #####, widen the column.
Task 8 (level 2) The foreman adds four more studs. First save a copy as v2 and confirm it is open. Change B2 from 48 to 52. Which cells changed by themselves? Write their new values. Save as v2.
Check yourself
What must every Excel formula start with?
What is in cell C4 of the practice table?
Does =2+3*4 give 20 or 14? Why?
What does =SUM(B2:B5) do?
Why use a formula for a line total instead of typing the answer?

lessons.title: Email, calendar invites and video calls
lessons.text:
Write a clear work email with an attachment, put a meeting in your calendar, answer an invitation and join a Teams video call ready to talk.
Steps checked in the new Outlook for Windows and Microsoft Teams on Windows 11, 2026-11-06. Classic Outlook, Gmail and phone apps have the same parts with different buttons. Scheduling a Teams meeting from Outlook needs a work or school Microsoft 365 account.
Why this matters on the job
Employers, unions and training programs in BC send job offers, start dates, safety orientations and interview times by email and calendar invite. Many interviews and apprenticeship check-ins now happen on video. A clear email and a smooth video call tell an employer you are organized before you ever pick up a tool.
Key ideas
Your email address
For job applications, use an address with your name in it, such as jordan.lee@.... ACCESS has advised this since its first job-search lessons: employers often reply only to the address you applied from, and a nickname address can cost you the call.
The parts of an email
Part What goes in it
To The person who needs to act or answer
Cc People who should see it but do not need to act
Bcc People who get a copy without others seeing their address
Subject A short, specific line: what and when, such as Time sheet for week of Nov 2, Jordan Lee
Body Greeting, the point in the first line, details, what you need, your name
Attachment A file, such as a PDF of your time sheet
Signature Your name, trade or program, and phone number
Reply answers only the sender. Reply all answers everyone on the message. Use Reply all only when every person on the list needs your answer.
Write and send in the new Outlook
Select New > Mail, or press Ctrl + N.
Type the address in To (and Cc or Bcc if needed).
Type a subject in Add a subject.
Write the message.
To attach a file, select Insert > Attach file. If you mention an attachment and forget it, Outlook may warn you before sending.
Select Send.
To set up a signature: Settings > Accounts > Signatures > Add signature, type it, Save.
Calendar events and invitations
To put a meeting in your calendar in the new Outlook:
Go to Calendar and select New event.
Add a title.
Select Invite attendees to add people (or leave it empty for a personal reminder).
Set the date, start and end time.
Add a location. Turn on the Teams meeting toggle if it will be a video call (work or school accounts).
Select Send (or Save if no one is invited).
When someone invites you, the invitation offers Accept, Tentative and Decline. Answer it. If you just ignore it, the organizer cannot tell whether you are coming.
Joining a Teams call
Open the meeting from your Teams or Outlook calendar and select Join, or select the join link in the invitation email.
If you do not have a Teams account and the organizer allows it, you can type your name and join.
On the screen before you join, check your camera and microphone. Select Effects and avatars to blur your background (Standard blur or Portrait blur). Blur may not hide everything behind you, so check what the camera can see.
During the meeting, the controls bar has:
Control Use it to
Mic Mute and unmute yourself
Camera Turn your video on and off
Raise (or React > Raise hand) Show you want to speak without interrupting
Chat Type a question or share a link
Share Show your screen, a window or a PowerPoint file
Leave Leave the meeting
Good habits: mute when you are not talking, join a few minutes early, check what the camera shows behind you, and mute smart speakers, TV or music nearby.
Worked example
Jordan is a fictional ACCESS learner with a carpentry interview on Thursday at 10:00 a.m. The employer's email asks Jordan to confirm and bring a résumé.
Jordan replies (Reply, not Reply all):
Subject: RE: Interview Thursday 10:00 a.m., Jordan Lee
Hello Ms. Grant,
Thank you for the invitation. I confirm I will attend the interview on Thursday at 10:00 a.m. My résumé is attached as a PDF.
Jordan Lee Carpentry Foundation learner, ACCESS Indigenous Skills4Success 604-555-0137
Then Jordan accepts the calendar invite, so the interview shows in the calendar with a reminder.
Practice
Use the practice account and addresses your instructor gives you. Send messages only to your instructor or your own address. Do not use real employer addresses.
Task 1 (level 1) Rewrite each subject line so the reader knows what the email is about.
hi __________
question __________
stuff for monday __________
Task 2 (level 2) Write an email to your instructor's practice address. Your fictional foreman asked for your time sheet for this week. Use a clear subject, a greeting, one or two sentences, and your name. Attach a PDF from Lesson 4 as if it were your time sheet. Send it.
Task 3 (level 1) Your instructor sends one email to the whole class asking: "Who can stay late Friday for cleanup? Reply to me only." Do you use Reply or Reply all? Reply with your answer.
Task 4 (level 2) Put this in your calendar: Site safety orientation, next Monday 7:00 a.m. to 8:30 a.m. in the training site's time zone (agree the exact date and zone with your instructor), location Riverbend Builders yard (fictional). Add a reminder note in the body: Bring steel-toe boots and hard hat.
Task 5 (level 1) Your instructor will send you a calendar invitation. Answer it with Accept, Tentative or Decline, and say why you chose that one.
Task 6 (level 2) Join the practice Teams meeting from the invitation. Before you join: blur your background and check your mic. In the meeting: unmute, say your name, mute again, raise your hand, type Ready in the chat, then lower your hand.
Task 7 (level 2) In the practice meeting, share one window (your Lesson 4 PDF) for ten seconds, then stop sharing. Tell the group one thing to close or hide before sharing your screen at work.
Check yourself
What is the difference between Cc and Bcc?
When should you use Reply all?
Why should you answer a calendar invitation instead of ignoring it?
What does background blur not guarantee?
Which control do you use to ask to speak without interrupting?

lessons.title: Search and judge online information
lessons.text:
Search with quotes, site and minus to get better results, read a web address to see who really runs the page, and check whether information is current before you rely on it.
Search tips checked against Google Search Help, 2026-11-06. Bing and other search engines accept similar operators, but check their help pages. Any web browser works for this lesson.
Why this matters on the job
Before you start a job you may need the current safety rule, the right form, a supplier's spec sheet or an employer's application page. The first search result is not always the right one: it can be an old copy, a forum post, an ad or a fake site built to look official. In the trades, acting on the wrong version of a rule can cost money or get someone hurt.
Key ideas
Read the web address
A web address (URL) is the location of a page. Example:
https://www.worksafebc.com/en/health-safety/hazards-exposures/ergonomics
https:// means the connection is encrypted. It does not prove the site is honest.
www.worksafebc.com is the domain: the site host name. The registered domain and the organization behind it need checking.
Everything after the first single / is the page inside that site.
To find the real owner, look at the part just before the first single /, and read it from the right. The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security warns that fake sites use addresses like login.google.com.example.com. That page belongs to example.com, not Google.
Examples of official addresses you will use in these lessons:
Exact domain or a subdomain of it Organization to check
canada.ca or .gc.ca (for example cyber.gc.ca) Government of Canada
gov.bc.ca Government of British Columbia
worksafebc.com WorkSafeBC
vancouver.ca City of Vancouver
Check the hostname, not words later in the URL. For example, notcanada.ca is not canada.ca, and example.com/canada.ca is still on example.com. Read the suspicious examples below as text only; do not visit them.
Search smarter
Google Search Help lists these operators. Do not put a space after the colon.
Type this It finds Example
"words in quotes" that exact phrase "confined space"
site: results only from one site ladder safety site:worksafebc.com
-word results without that word pipe threading -plastic
filetype: one kind of file computer workstation filetype:pdf
before: and after: pages updated before or after a date scaffold after:2025
Judge what you find
Ask five questions about any page:
Who made it? Look at the domain and the "About" page.
When was it updated? Government of Canada pages show "Date modified" at the bottom. Many guides show a publication date.
Does it answer my question, for BC, for my trade, today?
Is it the source, or someone repeating the source? A blog about a WorkSafeBC rule is not the rule.
Can I confirm it in a second trusted place?
Some results are paid ads, and they can look like normal results. Check the label and the address before you click.
Worked example
Kai needs WorkSafeBC's guide on setting up a computer workstation.
Kai searches computer workstation guide site:worksafebc.com. Every result is now from WorkSafeBC.
Kai opens How to Make Your Computer Workstation Fit You.
Kai checks the address starts with www.worksafebc.com/ and reads the publication details: May 2023, publication BK76.
Kai writes a source note: title, publisher, date, address, date checked.
Practice
Task 1 (level 1) For each address, write the site host name. The registered domain and the organization behind it need checking.
https://www.canada.ca/en/services/jobs/training/initiatives/skills-success.html __
https://www.cyber.gc.ca/en/guidance/best-practices-passphrases-and-passwords-itsap30032 __
https://worksafebc.com.safety-update.net/login __
Task 2 (level 1) Search Skills for Success Digital site:canada.ca. Open the Government of Canada page Skill components and proficiency levels. Copy the one-sentence definition of Digital.
Task 3 (level 2) Search computer workstation fit you site:worksafebc.com. Find the guide in the worked example. Write its publication date and publication number.
Task 4 (level 2) You search for a fall protection rule and get these three results. Rank them from most to least trustworthy for a BC job site and give a reason for each.
Result Address shown
A. "Fall protection rules explained: my 20 years on the tools" https://tradesguyblog.example.com/fall-rules
B. "Fall protection, Occupational Health and Safety Regulation" https://www.worksafebc.com/...
C. "Sponsored: Buy fall arrest kits, BC approved!" https://deals.example-safety-shop.com/
Task 5 (level 2) Open the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre page at https://antifraudcentre-centreantifraude.ca/report-signalez-eng.htm. Scroll to the bottom. Write the "Date modified". Then write the toll-free phone number on the page.
Task 6 (level 2) Run the same search twice and compare the first three results: ladder and then ladder inspection site:worksafebc.com. Write what changed and why.
Check yourself
Does https:// prove a site is official?
Who really owns login.google.com.example.com?
What does site:worksafebc.com do in a search?
Where do Government of Canada pages show when they were last changed?
Why is a blog about a safety rule weaker evidence than the rule itself?

lessons.title: Passwords, passkeys and phishing
lessons.text:
Make strong passphrases, use multi-factor authentication and passkeys, spot phishing emails, texts, calls and QR codes, and know where to report a scam.
Guidance checked against the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (cyber.gc.ca) and the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre, 2026-11-06. It applies to any phone, tablet or computer.
Why this matters on the job
Your work email, pay stub site, union account and ticket records all sit behind a sign-in. If someone steals that sign-in, they can redirect your pay, send fake orders in your name or lock you out. Scammers also target trades workers with fake job offers, fake supplier invoices and texts that look like they come from payroll. A few habits stop most of this.
Key ideas
Passphrases and passwords
The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (the Cyber Centre) recommends a passphrase: a string of mixed words you can remember.
At least 4 words and 15 characters, with or without spaces.
One way to build one: look around a room and pick unrelated words for things you see.
If a site will not take a passphrase, use a password of at least 12 characters with upper and lower case letters, numbers and special characters.
The Cyber Centre also says:
Use a different passphrase for each account, especially email and banking.
Do not share it, even with family. Do not give it out by phone or online.
Do not use your birthday, hometown, pet's name, song lyrics, or anything like password or 1234, even with tricks like p@ssword.
Do not type passwords on public Wi-Fi.
Sign out when you finish on a shared computer.
A password manager can create and remember passwords for you. The Cyber Centre says to protect it with a strong passphrase and multi-factor authentication, keep it updated, and not use it for your most sensitive accounts, such as banking.
Multi-factor authentication (MFA)
MFA means you need two or more different things to sign in:
something you know (a passphrase or PIN)
something you have (your phone or a security key)
something you are (a fingerprint or face)
So a stolen password alone is not enough. Turn MFA on for email, banking and any work account. If you get a sign-in approval request you did not start, deny it: it may mean someone is trying to access your account. Treat it as suspicious and report it; the prompt alone does not prove how it was triggered. Some MFA asks you to match a number shown on screen, which helps stop that trick. The Cyber Centre suggests avoiding text-message (SMS) codes as an MFA method where a better option is offered.
Passkeys
A passkey replaces the password. It is a digital key stored on your device and unlocked with your fingerprint, face or PIN. The website never gets a password to steal, and passkeys resist phishing because a fake site cannot use them. Many accounts still keep a password as a backup way in, so that password still needs to be strong.
Phishing
Phishing is a message that looks real but is built to make you give up information, click a bad link, open a bad attachment or send money. It comes as:
email (phishing)
text message (smishing)
phone call (vishing), sometimes with an AI-made voice that sounds like someone you know
QR code (quishing), on a poster, a parking meter or in an email
The Cyber Centre says something may be "phishy" if:
it is urgent and has a deadline
it asks for personal or confidential information
it asks you to sign in through a link it gives you
the offer sounds too good to be true
you did not ask for it and it has an attachment, link, QR code or sign-in page, or claims to be the government or a bank
you do not recognize the sender. Addresses can be faked, so a known name is not proof.
Spelling mistakes used to be a giveaway. With AI, many scam messages are now well written, so check the other signs.
What to do
Stay calm. Scams depend on rushing you.
Do not click, scan, reply or call the number in the message.
Check through a separate channel. If "the bank" calls, hang up and call your branch from the number on your card or the bank's website. If "payroll" emails, phone or walk over to payroll.
Report it. At work, tell your supervisor or IT. For fraud, report to the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre at reportcyberandfraud.canada.ca or 1-888-495-8501. If you lost money or information, also contact your local police as soon as possible.
Worked example
Tanis gets this text: RIVERBEND PAYROLL: Your direct deposit failed. Update your bank info in 2 hrs or miss this pay: [link].
Signs: urgent deadline, asks for banking information, sends a sign-in link, unexpected. Tanis does not tap the link. She phones the Riverbend office number on her pay stub. Payroll says no message was sent. Tanis forwards a screenshot to her supervisor and deletes the text.
Practice
Never type a real password, PIN or security answer in class. Use invented examples only.
Task 1 (level 1) Build a practice passphrase using the room method. Write four unrelated words for things you can see in this room, then count the characters including spaces. Do not use it for a real account.
Words: _____ Characters: ____
Task 2 (level 1) Rate each practice password as strong or weak, using the Cyber Centre guidance, and give one reason.
Fluffy2009 ____
p@ssword123 ____
gravel kettle spruce lantern ____
1234 ____
Task 3 (level 2) Your phone shows a sign-in approval request for your work email at 2:00 a.m. You were asleep and did not try to sign in. What do you do, and what does the request tell you?
Task 4 (level 2) List every phishing sign in this fictional email.
From: Riverbend Builders HR <hr-riverbend@quick-mail-help.example> Subject: FINAL NOTICE: confirm your SIN today
Your employment file is incomplete. Click the secure link below and enter your Social Insurance Number and banking details within 24 hours or your position will be cancelled.
Task 5 (level 2) A poster on the site trailer door says Scan for your new safety orientation schedule with a QR code taped over another code. What could be wrong, and what would you do instead?
Task 6 (level 1) A caller says they are from your bank and asks you to read back a code that was just texted to you. Write the steps you take, in order.
Check yourself
How long should a passphrase be, according to the Cyber Centre?
Name the three kinds of factors in multi-factor authentication.
Why can a fake website not steal a passkey the way it steals a password?
Name three signs that a message may be phishing.
Where do you report a fraud in Canada?

lessons.title: Find and measure a site on a map
lessons.text:
Find a job site by address and by coordinates, measure a distance, look up property and zoning information in VanMap, and know what an online map cannot tell you before you dig.
Checked in Google Maps on a computer (web browser) and the City of Vancouver's new VanMap Viewer, 2026-11-06. The older public VanMap Viewer was scheduled to be retired in the third quarter of 2026, so use the new one. On a phone, Google Maps uses touch and hold instead of right-click.
Why this matters on the job
Crews get sent to new addresses every week, and some sites have no street number yet, only a lot or a set of coordinates. Estimators measure how far a run of fence or pipe goes before they visit. Contractors check a property's zoning before they quote. Online maps make all of this faster, but they are not surveys, and they do not show what is buried underground.
Key ideas
Latitude and longitude
A point on Earth can be written as two numbers:
Latitude: how far north or south of the equator. In BC it is a positive number, because BC is north of the equator.
Longitude: how far east or west. In BC it is a negative number, because BC is west of Greenwich, England.
Google Maps writes them in decimal degrees, latitude first, with a comma between: for example 49.2610, -123.1139. Use a period for the decimal, never a comma.
Google Maps on a computer
Find coordinates: right-click the place on the map. The latitude and longitude appear at the top of the pop-up. Click them to copy.
Go to coordinates: type them in the search box.
Measure a straight line: right-click the starting point, choose Measure distance, then click each next point. The total shows at the bottom in miles and kilometres. Measuring does not work in Lite mode.
A measured straight line is not the driving distance. Roads bend.
VanMap (City of Vancouver)
VanMap is the City of Vancouver's map site at maps.vancouver.ca. Its VanMap Viewer (vanmapviewer.vancouver.ca) shows property, zoning, water and sewer information and aerial photos for addresses in Vancouver. You must agree to the VanMap Terms of Use before it opens.
The Viewer has tools for:
Tool Use it to
Property Viewer Report See details about a property, including its zoning
Map Layers Turn layers of information on and off
Legend See what the colours and symbols mean
Measurement Measure approximate lengths and areas
Draw Mark up the map
Basemap Gallery Switch between map and aerial views
Print Print or save the map
The City says its map measurements are approximate and that only a BC Land Surveyor can verify property measurements. The City's Digital Zoning Map also warns that the map is a snapshot and may not be accurate when you view it. Other BC cities and regional districts have their own map sites with similar tools.
What no online map tells you: buried lines
Before anyone digs, even for a fence post, BC 1 Call must be contacted for a "locate". It is free. Request online at bc1c.ca or call 1-800-474-6886. Members who own buried lines respond with instructions, within 3 business days for a standard request, and you must not dig until you have every response. An online map that shows a sewer line is not a locate.
Worked example
A foreman sends Sam the coordinates 49.2610, -123.1139 for a pickup.
Sam opens Google Maps and types 49.2610, -123.1139 in the search box. The pin lands at Vancouver City Hall, 453 West 12th Avenue.
Sam right-clicks the parking area entrance, chooses Measure distance, and clicks the front steps. The card at the bottom shows the straight-line distance.
The job is in Vancouver, so Sam opens the VanMap Viewer, agrees to the Terms of Use, searches 453 W 12th Ave, and opens the Property Viewer Report to see the zoning.
Practice
Task 1 (level 1) In Google Maps, find Vancouver City Hall, 453 West 12th Avenue. Right-click the building and write its latitude and longitude to four decimal places.
Task 2 (level 2) In Google Maps, use Measure distance to measure the straight-line distance from Vancouver City Hall to the nearest SkyTrain station you can see on the map. Then ask for walking directions between the same two points. Write both distances and explain why they differ.
Task 3 (level 2) Open the VanMap Viewer and agree to the Terms of Use. Search 453 W 12th Ave. Open the Property Viewer Report. Write the zoning shown for the property.
Task 4 (level 2) Use the Measurement tool in VanMap to measure one side of the City Hall property. Write the length and units. Then write the sentence you would add if you put this number in a quote for a client.
Task 5 (level 1) In VanMap, open Map Layers and turn on one water or sewer layer. Use the Legend to say what one symbol means.
Task 6 (level 2) A homeowner in Surrey hires your crew to put in eight fence posts along the back property line on Monday. The homeowner says, "I checked the city map, there are no pipes there." What do you tell them, and what do you do before Monday? List the information you would need ready.
Check yourself
Which comes first in Google Maps coordinates, latitude or longitude?
Why is the longitude for a BC site a negative number?
Is a Google Maps straight-line measurement the same as the driving distance?
Who can verify property measurements, according to the City of Vancouver?
What must happen before anyone digs on a BC job site?

lessons.title: Make and give a short presentation
lessons.text:
Build a four-slide PowerPoint about a tool or part from your trade, add speaker notes, check it for accessibility, learn one new feature from the help pages and present it in two minutes.
Try it in the visual practice studio
Plan a visual story with a clear beginning, middle and ending.
Try the storyboard activity
Steps checked in PowerPoint for Microsoft 365 on Windows 11, 2026-11-06. PowerPoint for the web and Mac have the same tabs.
Why this matters on the job
Lead hands run toolbox talks. Apprentices explain a repair to a journeyperson. Contractors pitch a job to a client or a band office. A few clear slides and two minutes of confident talking can do more than a page of text, and the same skills work in a Teams meeting when you share your screen.
Key ideas
A short presentation that works
One idea per slide. A heading and a few words or one picture. Put the details in your speaker notes, not on the slide.
Contrast. Dark text on a light background, or light on dark. Microsoft's tips warn against designs that pull attention away from the message.
Your own pictures. Use photos you took of your own work or tools, or no picture. Do not copy pictures or company logos from websites.
Say where facts came from. If you state a safety rule or a spec, name the source on the last slide, such as the manufacturer's manual or a WorkSafeBC page.
Building it
To do this In PowerPoint
Start with a design File > New, choose a theme, Create
Add a slide Home, select the arrow on New Slide, choose a layout
Duplicate or delete a slide Right-click it in the thumbnail pane on the left
Move a slide Drag it in the thumbnail pane
Add speaker notes Select Notes at the bottom of the window, type in the Notes pane
Save File > Save, pick the folder, type a name
Checking it
Review > Check Accessibility lists problems such as pictures with no alternative text (alt text). Alt text is a short description that a screen reader reads aloud. Select an item in the list to see the recommended fix. Good alt text says what the picture shows and why it is there, in a sentence or less.
Presenting it
Slide Show > From Beginning, or press F5.
Press N for the next slide, P for the previous slide, Esc to stop.
With Use Presenter View ticked on the Slide Show tab and a second screen connected, you see your notes and the next slide while the audience sees only the current slide.
In a Teams meeting, select Share and choose the PowerPoint file.
Learning a feature nobody taught you
Apps change every year. When you need something new, search the vendor's own help site, for example slide numbers site:support.microsoft.com, read the steps for your version, try them on a copy, and check the result.
Worked example
Rae is a fictional millwright learner. Her topic is a dial indicator.
File > New, a plain theme with high contrast, Create.
Slide 1: The dial indicator and Rae M., ACCESS Indigenous Skills4Success.
Slide 2: What it measures, one photo she took of her own indicator, and notes explaining it in her own words.
Slide 3: How I set it up, three short steps.
Slide 4: Source: the maker's instruction sheet that came with her indicator.
Review > Check Accessibility flags the photo. She adds alt text: Dial indicator on a magnetic base, needle touching a shaft.
She presses F5 and practises out loud with a timer.
Practice
Task 1 (level 1) Choose a tool, part or process from your trade, for example a chalk line, a pipe wrench, a torch tip or a ladder inspection. Write your topic and where you will get your facts.
Topic: ____ Source: ____
Task 2 (level 1) Make a new presentation from a theme. Add four slides: a title slide with your topic and name, two content slides, and a source slide. Save it as presentation_[topic]_[initials]_v1 in your practice folder.
Task 3 (level 2) Write speaker notes for slides 2 and 3: what you will say, in two or three sentences each. Keep the slides themselves to a heading and no more than about 15 words.
Task 4 (level 2) Run Review > Check Accessibility. Fix every item it lists, or write "no issues found".
Task 5 (level 2) Pick one PowerPoint feature this lesson did not teach, such as slide numbers, a footer or a transition. Find the steps on support.microsoft.com, try them on your slides, and write the page title you used and whether it worked.
Task 6 (level 1) Start the slide show with F5. Move forward with N and back with P. Press Esc to stop.
Task 7 (level 2) Explain what the tool, part or process is, how it is used, and one safety or quality point supported by your source. Give your presentation to your group in two minutes or less. Ask one person to time you and one person to tell you one thing that worked and one thing to change.
Check yourself
Where do the details go, on the slide or in the notes?
How do you start a slide show from the first slide?
What is alt text for?
Which key ends a slide show?
You need a PowerPoint feature you have never used. Where do you look first?

lessons.title: How AI chatbots work
lessons.text:
Learn what a large language model is, why a chatbot can sound sure and still be wrong, and how to check an AI answer against the official source.
Facts about how these tools work were checked against help pages from Google, OpenAI and Anthropic, and the safety rule against the WorkSafeBC website, on 2026-11-06. This lesson applies to any AI chatbot. Lessons 12 to 15 cover four products one at a time.
Why this matters on the job
AI chatbots such as Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot and Gemini can write a materials list, explain a regulation in plain words or help you word a message to your foreman. They answer fast and they sound sure. They can also be wrong. On a job site, a wrong height, quantity or rule can cost money or get someone hurt. If you know how the tool makes an answer, you know when and how to check it.
Key ideas
What a large language model is
A large language model (LLM) is the engine inside an AI chatbot.
It was trained on a very large amount of text. During training it learned patterns: which words tend to follow which other words.
It does not store that text like a filing cabinet or a database. Do not treat it as a reliable archive or an exact copy of a source.
When you ask a question, it predicts the next word, then the next, then the next, until the answer is done. Google gives this example: after "think outside the", the word "box" is more likely than "blue".
Tokens
The model does not read whole words. It reads tokens: small pieces of text. A token can be one letter, part of a word or a whole word. Spaces and punctuation count too.
OpenAI gives these rules of thumb for English text:
1 token is about 4 characters
100 tokens is about 75 words
Other languages often use more tokens for the same number of characters. Each chatbot has a limit on how much text it can hold in one conversation, and that limit is counted in tokens. A very long chat or a very large file can push early details out.
The model and the app are different things
What it is Example
Model The trained engine that predicts text The model behind Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot or Gemini
App The website or phone app you type into claude.ai, chatgpt.com, the Copilot app, the Gemini app
The app adds tools around the model. Depending on the product, your plan and your settings, the app can:
search the web
read a file or photo you upload
remember things from past chats (memory)
create files, images or code
So two people using the "same" chatbot can get different results. One may have web search or memory turned on, and the other may not.
Why it can sound sure and still be wrong
The model picks likely words. Likely is not the same as true. OpenAI's help page says ChatGPT can sound confident even when it is wrong. Google says the same about all large language models, Gemini included. Common mistakes:
wrong numbers, dates or definitions
made-up quotes, sources or section numbers
a rule from another province or country presented as if it applies in BC
an old version of a rule
When a chatbot invents something, people call it a hallucination.
Knowledge cutoff and web search
A model only learned from text up to a certain date. This is its knowledge cutoff. It does not know about changes after that date unless the app uses a tool such as web search.
With web search on, the app looks up pages and the model writes an answer from them. Good apps show links. Open the links: the answer can still misread the page.
With web search off, the model can still use the conversation, uploaded files and other context the app supplies, as well as training patterns. That context is not automatically current or correct. For anything that changes (wages, rules, prices, forms, schedules), go to the official site.
Check what information the app can use
A chatbot may receive information about you from what you type, uploaded files, saved memory, connected apps or work files that it has permission to access. It may also infer details from context. Turning memory off is not a guarantee that the app has no information about you. Check the account, connections and content before using it.
Each product has settings to see, turn off or delete memory. Lessons 12 to 15 show where. Treat anything you type as something that may be stored. Lesson 16 covers what never to paste.
Good and bad jobs for a chatbot on a job site
Good jobs (you still check) Poor jobs (do not rely on it)
Turn your notes into a clear message Deciding if a scaffold or ladder is safe
Explain a regulation in plain words, with the source open beside it Telling you the current rule without a source
Make a first list of materials from your measurements Final quantities for an order without your own math
Practise for an interview or a ticket exam Medical, legal or emergency decisions
Rewrite a long email shorter Anything that needs a licensed person to sign off
Worked example: check an AI answer against WorkSafeBC
Jordan, a first-year carpentry apprentice, asks a chatbot: "When do I need fall protection on a job site in BC?"
The chatbot answers: "In BC you need fall protection when working at 3 m (10 ft) or higher."
Jordan checks it with the check-it loop:
What is the claim? Fall protection is needed at 3 m (10 ft) or more.
Find the official source. Rules for BC workplaces are in the WorkSafeBC Occupational Health and Safety Regulation. Jordan searches fall protection site:worksafebc.com and opens Part 11, Fall Protection, at worksafebc.com.
Compare. Section 11.2(1) says the employer must make sure a fall protection system is used where a fall of 3 m (10 ft) or more may occur. It also covers falls from less than 3 m where the risk of injury is greater than landing on a flat surface. The chatbot left out that second part.
Decide. The number was right. The answer was incomplete. Jordan writes his own note: "Fall protection at 3 m or more, or lower where landing would be worse than a flat surface. OHS Regulation s. 11.2(1), worksafebc.com, checked 2026-11-06."
Ask your supervisor how it applies on your site. The employer must instruct workers in the fall protection system for the area before they go there (s. 11.2(6)).
Practice
You do not need an AI account for Tasks 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6. Task 4 needs a web browser.
Task 1 (level 1) Match each word to its meaning. Write the letter.
Word Letter Meaning
1. Prompt ___ A. The trained engine that predicts text
2. Token ___ B. The date the model's training text stops
3. Model ___ C. What you type or say to the chatbot
4. Knowledge cutoff ___ D. A setting that lets the app keep details from past chats
5. Memory ___ E. A small piece of text the model reads
6. Hallucination ___ F. An answer the chatbot made up
Task 2 (level 1) Write G for a good job for a chatbot (you still check it) or P for a poor job.
a. Turn your rough notes about a late delivery into a short, polite text to your foreman. ___
b. Tell you if the guardrail on a third-floor deck is strong enough. ___
c. Explain the word "anchorage" in plain language. ___
d. Give you today's BC minimum wage with web search turned off. ___
e. Quiz you on the parts of a framing square. ___
Task 3 (level 2) Use OpenAI's rule of thumb: 100 tokens is about 75 words. A safety talk handout has 600 words. About how many tokens is that? Show your math.
Task 4 (level 2) A chatbot says: "In BC, a worker can decide not to use the fall protection the employer gives them if they feel safe." Use the check-it loop. Open Part 11 of the OHS Regulation at https://www.worksafebc.com/en/law-policy/occupational-health-safety/searchable-ohs-regulation/ohs-regulation/part-11-fall-protection and find section 11.2. Is the answer right? Write the section number that settles it.
Task 5 (level 2) You ask a chatbot with web search turned off: "What is the minimum wage in BC today?" Explain why this answer could be out of date, and write two better ways to get the current figure.
Task 6 (level 1) For each case, write Yes or No: could the chatbot know this about you?
a. Your employer's name, in a new chat with memory off, no connected apps or files, and no identifying information in the chat or account context. ___
b. Your trade, if you told it last week and memory is on. ___
c. Your street address, if it was in a résumé you uploaded in this chat. ___
Check yourself
In your own words, how does a large language model write an answer?
What is the difference between the model and the app?
Why can a chatbot sound sure and still be wrong?
What does web search change, and what does it not change?
Name the five steps of the check-it loop.

lessons.title: Using Claude
lessons.text:
Get started with Anthropic's Claude, find its privacy settings, and use it for a materials list, a code explanation and a message to your foreman, checking each answer.
Product facts on this page were checked against Anthropic's own pages (claude.com, support.claude.com and privacy.claude.com) on 2026-11-06. Claude changes often. Your instructor checks the help page again before class.
Why this matters on the job
Claude is an AI chatbot you can use on a computer or phone to explain a document, word a message or work through a materials list. Some employers give workers Claude through a work plan. Knowing where its settings are, and what it can and cannot do, helps you use it safely and check its work before it reaches a job site.
Key ideas
Who makes it and how to get it
Made by Anthropic.
Web: claude.ai in any browser.
Computer app: Claude Desktop for Mac or Windows.
Phone app: Claude for iOS or Android.
Account: you sign up with an email address. You must be at least 18 and in a location Anthropic supports.
Plans for one person: Free, Pro, Max and Ultra. Plans for organizations: Team and Enterprise.
The Free plan has usage limits that reset every 5 hours and every week.
Price: Anthropic's pricing page shows prices in US dollars and says local pricing applies where supported. Check claude.ai/upgrade or your phone's app store for the price in Canada. You do not need a paid plan for this lesson.
Official help page: Claude Help Center, Get started with Claude, https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8114491-get-started-with-claude
What it can do
Anthropic's plan page lists these for the Free plan:
chat on the web, the computer app and the phone app
search the web
create files and run code
memory across conversations
connect your apps and tools
You can also:
upload documents (such as PDF, Word .docx, CSV and plain text) and images (JPEG, PNG, GIF and WebP), up to 20 files in one chat
use voice mode to talk with Claude and hear it answer. Voice mode is in beta on all plans and is built to work best in the phone app.
Features depend on your plan, your device and where you live. If you do not see a feature, check the help page.
Where you may meet it at work
Organizations can buy Claude Team or Enterprise plans. On those plans, the organization's owners control some settings, such as whether memory is available.
Anthropic's plan page lists Claude in Chrome and Microsoft 365 as part of the Pro plan.
If your employer gives you Claude through work, use the work account for work only and follow your employer's AI policy (Lesson 16).
Privacy and data settings
Model improvement. On the web: select your name, then Settings > Privacy, then the switch under Help improve our AI models. The phone app uses the same path. This switch controls whether Anthropic may use your chats to train future models. If it is on, Anthropic may keep your chats in a de-identified form for up to 5 years for training.
Incognito chats. When you start a new chat, a ghost icon at the top right turns on incognito. It is on all plans. Anthropic says incognito chats are not used to improve Claude, even when model improvement is on.
Memory is on by default on Free, Pro, Max and Ultra. To see, edit or turn it off, go to Settings > Memory. In the newer settings layout, go to Settings > Your Claude and select Manage next to Your memory. Anthropic says Claude does not save sensitive topics, such as health or religion, to memory unless you turn that on.
Deleting a chat removes it from your chat history right away and from Anthropic's back-end storage within 30 days. Chats flagged by Anthropic's safety systems can be kept longer.
Whatever the settings, do not paste your Social Insurance Number, health information, client names and addresses, or your employer's private information into any chatbot. Lesson 16 covers this in detail.
Limits
Like every large language model (Lesson 11), Claude can give wrong numbers, wrong rules or made-up sources in a confident voice.
The Free plan's usage limit can stop you partway through a task. Use the instructor demonstration or wait for the reset described in the current help page. Starting another chat is not a reliable way to restore an account usage allowance.
Claude does not know your job site, your employer or your trade unless you tell it or memory saved it.
A prompt pattern that works
Give Claude five things:
Who you are. "I am a first-year carpentry apprentice in BC."
The facts. Measurements, quantities and the situation. Leave out private details.
What you want. "Make a materials list."
The format. "As a table." "In three short sentences." "Under 50 words."
Show the work. "Show your math." "Give the section number and a link to the official page."
Worked example: drywall sheets
Rae, a drywall apprentice, needs sheets for one side of a wall 4.8 m long and 2.4 m high, with no openings. For this fictional calculation, use sheets exactly 1.2 m by 2.4 m. These are practice metric dimensions, not an exact conversion of 4 ft by 8 ft. Check actual product dimensions before ordering.
Rae types: "I am a drywall apprentice in BC. One side of a wall is 4.8 m long and 2.4 m high, with no doors or windows. Sheets are 1.2 m by 2.4 m. How many sheets do I need? Show your math."
Claude's exact words change from day to day, so they are not printed here. Rae checks whatever it says with her own math:
Wall area: 4.8 × 2.4 = 11.52 m²
One sheet: 1.2 × 2.4 = 2.88 m²
Sheets: 11.52 ÷ 2.88 = 4
Another way: 4.8 ÷ 1.2 = 4 sheets standing side by side, each 2.4 m tall.
If Claude also says 4, Rae uses it. If it says something else, Rae trusts her own math and asks Claude to explain the difference. Before ordering, she asks her journeyperson whether to add extra for waste.
Practice
All quantities, sites and people in the practice prompts are fictional. The fence exercise assumes no gates or waste; two bags per post is supplied practice data, not a construction specification.
Do Tasks 3, 4 and 5 in Claude. If you do not have an account, your instructor shows Claude on the projector and you do the checking. Never type a real client's name, your SIN or your employer's private information.
Task 1 (level 1) Open the official help page (https://support.claude.com/en/articles/8114491-get-started-with-claude) and Claude's own website. Fill in the product card. Use only the company's own pages.
Question Your answer
Who makes it
Web address
Apps
Account you sign in with
Minimum age
Plan names
Two things it can do
Task 2 (level 1) Find two privacy settings. Write the menu path for each. Use the app if you have an account, or the help page if you do not. Do not change settings on a shared or work account without permission.
(a) A control or policy about chat retention or model training. State which one it affects; these are not the same. If no control is available, record that and the official help page: ______
(b) Where you see or delete what it remembers, or delete a chat: ______
Task 3 (level 2) Materials list. Type this prompt into Claude:
I am building a straight wood fence 21.6 m long. Posts go every 2.4 m, with a post at each end. Each section between posts gets 2 rails, each 2.4 m long. Each post needs 2 bags of concrete mix. Make a materials list with quantities. Show your math.
Then work it out yourself. Write the correct number of posts, rails and bags. Did Claude get the number of posts right?
Task 4 (level 2) Explain a code clause, then check it. Type:
In plain words for a first-year apprentice, explain what WorkSafeBC OHS Regulation section 11.2, subsections (2) to (5), say about choosing a type of fall protection. Put the options in order.
Then open Part 11 at https://www.worksafebc.com/en/law-policy/occupational-health-safety/searchable-ohs-regulation/ohs-regulation/part-11-fall-protection and read section 11.2. Write the correct order of the four options, and one thing Claude got right or wrong.
Task 5 (level 2) Message to your foreman. You are an apprentice with Northgate Framing Ltd. (a fictional company). At 7:10 a.m. the lumber delivery to the Alder Street site came with 40 studs. The packing slip says 60. Ask Claude to write a short, polite text to your foreman, Dale, that says what happened and asks what to do. Check the message: are the time and numbers right, is there no blame, is there one clear question, and is there nothing private in it? Write the message you would send.
Task 6 (level 1) Check-it card. Pick Task 3 or Task 4 and fill in the card.
Step Your answer
What Claude said (the claim)
Where I checked
Same or different
What I changed or kept
Check yourself
Who makes Claude, and where is its official help?
What account do you need, and what is the minimum age?
Name two things Claude can do.
Where is the setting that controls whether your chats are kept or used to improve the AI?
Why do you check Claude's answer to a materials or code question before you use it?

lessons.title: Using ChatGPT
lessons.text:
Get started with OpenAI's ChatGPT, find its data controls, and use it for a materials list, a code explanation and a message to your foreman, checking each answer.
Product facts on this page were checked against OpenAI's own pages (openai.com and help.openai.com) on 2026-11-06. ChatGPT changes often. Your instructor checks the help page again before class.
Why this matters on the job
ChatGPT is an AI chatbot from OpenAI. You can use it in a browser or a phone app to explain a rule, work through a materials list or word a message. Some employers give workers ChatGPT through a business plan. Knowing its settings helps you protect your own information and your employer's, and checking its work keeps mistakes off the job site.
Key ideas
Who makes it and how to get it
Made by OpenAI.
Web: chatgpt.com. Phone apps: iOS and Android.
In supported countries you can try ChatGPT before you make an account. Without an account, the chat is not saved. An account saves your chat history and lets you export your data.
OpenAI recommends a personal email address for personal use and a separate account with your work email for work.
Minimum age: 13. Anyone under 18 needs a parent's or guardian's permission.
Personal plans: Free, Go, Plus and Pro. Work plans: Business, Enterprise and Edu.
OpenAI says ads may appear on the Free plan in certain countries, and the Go plan may include ads.
Price: check openai.com/chatgpt/pricing for the price shown to you in Canada. You do not need a paid plan for this lesson.
Official help page: OpenAI Help Center, ChatGPT Free Tier FAQ, https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9275245-chatgpt-free-tier-faq
What it can do
OpenAI's help page lists these for the Free plan:
search the web for up-to-date information
upload images or files and ask about them
analyze data
create images
discover and use GPTs (versions of ChatGPT set up for one job)
store files in Library (500 MB on Free)
You can also use ChatGPT Voice to talk and hear spoken answers. Choose voice options in Settings > Voice. The Free plan has limited voice use.
Features depend on your plan, your device and where you live. If you do not see a feature, check the help page.
Where you may meet it at work
ChatGPT Business, Enterprise and Edu are workspaces run by an organization. OpenAI says that by default it does not use content from these workspaces to train its models.
One account can belong to more than one workspace. Check which workspace you are in before you type work information.
If your employer gives you ChatGPT through work, use the work workspace for work and follow your employer's AI policy (Lesson 16).
Privacy and data settings
Model training. On the web: open your account menu, select Settings > Data controls, then Improve the model for everyone. On the phone: open the sidebar, tap your profile icon, then Data controls. On personal Free, Plus and Pro accounts this is on by default. When it is off, new chats are not used to train OpenAI models, and they still stay in your history.
Temporary Chat. A temporary chat does not appear in your history, does not create or update memories and is not used to train models. OpenAI may keep it for up to 30 days for safety.
Memory. Go to Settings > Personalization. "Reference saved memories" covers details ChatGPT saved. "Reference chat history" lets it use past chats. Turning off saved memories also turns off chat history.
Your data. Signed-in Free, Go, Plus and Pro users can export their data or delete their account from settings.
Whatever the settings, do not paste your Social Insurance Number, health information, client names and addresses, or your employer's private information into any chatbot. Lesson 16 covers this in detail.
Limits
OpenAI says ChatGPT can give wrong facts, make up sources and sound confident even when it is wrong. It also has a knowledge cutoff unless it uses tools such as search.
Some tools on the Free plan have their own usage limits.
ChatGPT does not know your job site, your employer or your trade unless you tell it or memory saved it.
A prompt pattern that works
Give ChatGPT five things:
Who you are. "I am a first-year carpentry apprentice in BC."
The facts. Measurements, quantities and the situation. Leave out private details.
What you want. "Make a materials list."
The format. "As a table." "In three short sentences." "Under 50 words."
Show the work. "Show your math." "Give the section number and a link to the official page."
Worked example: drywall sheets
Rae, a drywall apprentice, needs sheets for one side of a wall 4.8 m long and 2.4 m high, with no openings. For this fictional calculation, use sheets exactly 1.2 m by 2.4 m. These are practice metric dimensions, not an exact conversion of 4 ft by 8 ft. Check actual product dimensions before ordering.
Rae types: "I am a drywall apprentice in BC. One side of a wall is 4.8 m long and 2.4 m high, with no doors or windows. Sheets are 1.2 m by 2.4 m. How many sheets do I need? Show your math."
ChatGPT's exact words change from day to day, so they are not printed here. Rae checks whatever it says with her own math:
Wall area: 4.8 × 2.4 = 11.52 m²
One sheet: 1.2 × 2.4 = 2.88 m²
Sheets: 11.52 ÷ 2.88 = 4
Another way: 4.8 ÷ 1.2 = 4 sheets standing side by side, each 2.4 m tall.
If ChatGPT also says 4, Rae uses it. If it says something else, Rae trusts her own math and asks ChatGPT to explain the difference. Before ordering, she asks her journeyperson whether to add extra for waste.
Practice
All quantities, sites and people in the practice prompts are fictional. The fence exercise assumes no gates or waste; two bags per post is supplied practice data, not a construction specification.
Do Tasks 3, 4 and 5 in ChatGPT. If you do not have an account, your instructor shows ChatGPT on the projector and you do the checking. Never type a real client's name, your SIN or your employer's private information.
